title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 3 Lesson 1: Passing Fixed Points custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A car travels along a straight road with constant acceleration $a$. It covers a distance of $40\text{ m}$ in a 2-second interval, and a distance of $52\text{ m}$ in the immediately following 2-second interval. Find the acceleration $a$ of the car.

A car travels along a straight road with constant acceleration. It covers $40\text{ m}$ during the first 2-second interval and $52\text{ m}$ during the next 2-second interval. Find the speed of the car at the instant between the two intervals (at $t = 2\text{ s}$).
A particle accelerates uniformly from rest at $4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ along a straight line. Find the distance travelled by the particle during its 5th second of motion.

A particle travels along a straight line with constant acceleration. It passes point $A$ with speed $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and point $B$ with speed $17\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Find the speed of the particle as it passes $M$.

A car accelerates uniformly along a straight road. It passes point $A$ with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and point $B$ with speed $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$, taking $4\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$. Find the distance $AB$.
A particle passes fixed point $P$ with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and passes fixed point $Q$ with speed $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The distance $PQ$ is $40\text{ m}$. Find the acceleration of the particle.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ moves in a straight line with constant acceleration through three collinear points $A, B$, and $C$. The distance $AB$ is $48\text{ m}$ and the distance $BC$ is $72\text{ m}$. The particle takes $4\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$, and also takes $4\text{ s}$ to travel from $B$ to $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the acceleration of $P$ is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and find the speed of $P$ as it passes point $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The particle continues to accelerate at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and passes a fourth collinear point $D$ with speed $33\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the distance $CD$.

questions.prompt: A cyclist travels along a straight road with constant acceleration $a$, passing through collinear points $A, B$, and $C$ in that order. The cyclist takes $2\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$ and $2\text{ s}$ to travel from $B$ to $C$. The cyclist passes through $B$ with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The distance $AB$ is $\frac{2}{3}$ of the distance $BC$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the cyclist.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance $AC$ and the speed of the cyclist as they pass point $A$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ travels along a straight line with constant acceleration $a$. The particle travels a distance of $34\text{ m}$ during the 3rd second of its motion and a distance of $46\text{ m}$ during the 6th second of its motion.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the initial speed $u$ and the acceleration $a$ of $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance travelled by $P$ during the first $8\text{ s}$ of its motion, and find the speed of $P$ at $t = 8\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A car travels along a straight road with constant acceleration $a$. It passes through collinear points $P, Q, R$, and $S$ in that order. The times taken to travel from $P$ to $Q$, from $Q$ to $R$, and from $R$ to $S$ are each equal to $5\text{ s}$. The distance $QR$ is $1.5$ times the distance $PQ$. At point $Q$, the speed of the car is $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the acceleration of the car is $1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and find the distance $PQ$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance $QS$ and the average speed of the car between $Q$ and $S$.

questions.prompt: A vehicle moves along a straight test track with constant acceleration $a$. It passes three marker posts $A, B$, and $C$. The distance $AB$ is $55\text{ m}$ and the vehicle takes $5\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$. The distance $BC$ is $80\text{ m}$ and the vehicle takes $4\text{ s}$ to travel from $B$ to $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the vehicle and its speed as it passes marker post $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the vehicle at marker post $C$, and calculate the additional distance the vehicle travels after passing $C$ before reaching a speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ moves along a straight horizontal track with constant acceleration $a$. It passes point $A$ with speed $u$ and point $B$ with speed $v$, where $v > u > 0$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the speed of $P$ as it passes the midpoint $M$ is given by $v_M = \sqrt{\frac{u^2 + v^2}{2}}$, and prove that $v_M > \frac{u + v}{2}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the particle passes $A$ with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and passes $B$ with speed $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$, taking $6\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$, find the time taken for $P$ to travel from $A$ to the midpoint $M$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A train travels between two stations $A$ and $D$ along a straight horizontal track. The train passes station $A$ with speed $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and accelerates uniformly for $10\text{ s}$ until passing marker $B$. From $B$, it travels a further distance of $400\text{ m}$ to marker $C$ with a different constant acceleration. The train passes $C$ with speed $28\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After passing $C$, the brakes are applied and the train decelerates uniformly at $1.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until coming to rest at station $D$. The total time taken from $A$ to $D$ is $46\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the train as it passes marker $B$, the acceleration during the first stage, and the distance $AB$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the train between $B$ and $C$, the total distance from $A$ to $D$, and the average speed of the train for the complete journey.
